What is the horizontal component of the force shown?
20 N
53°
horizontal
A
12 N
B
16 N
C
20 N
D
27 N

hints: Notice the $20 \text{ N}$ arrow makes $53^{\circ}$ with the dashed horizontal line, so the horizontal side is adjacent to the angle.
Recall that adjacent component equals magnitude times cosine of the angle: $F_x = F \cos \theta$.
Use $\cos 53^{\circ} \approx 0.6$ and multiply by $20 \text{ N}$ to find the horizontal value in newtons.
walkthrough: Identify the given vector: magnitude $F = 20 \text{ N}$ at $\theta = 53^{\circ}$ above the horizontal.
State the resolution rule: the component adjacent to the angle uses cosine, so $F_{horizontal} = F \cos \theta$.
Check that a component must be smaller than $20 \text{ N}$, which $12 \text{ N}$ satisfies, while $16 \text{ N}$ would be the vertical $20 \sin 53^{\circ}$ component. This is option A

B.explanation: This is the vertical component $20 \sin 53^{\circ} \approx 16 \text{ N}$, not the horizontal component.

C.explanation: This is the magnitude of the full $20 \text{ N}$ force, not its resolved horizontal part.

D.explanation: This value is larger than the $20 \text{ N}$ force and cannot be a component of it.
